solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A wild animal died on boat

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A wild beast has perished on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard means being on a ship or other vessel, a plain synonym of being on a boat.

clue.text: Insurance agent almost penniless?

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an insurance broker arranges policies for clients

explanation.surface: Asks whether an insurance salesman is nearly out of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Broke is informal for having no money at all, the same as being without a penny.

clue.text: Sinatra dancing for skilled worker

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters of the singer's name moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra dances in place of a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a craftsperson, someone doing skilled manual work.

clue.text: Creature oddly doomed

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of the word doomed

explanation.surface: An animal is strangely fated to die.
explanation.definitionFit: A doe is a female deer or rabbit, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Cook sounds like a donkey, you say?

indicators.note: you say signals that the word is spoken aloud, giving its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a donkey's cry is a bray, so one who sounds like a donkey brays

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cook's voice resembles a donkey's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds like' tempts as the homophone signal, but it is part of the wordplay's meaning (brays); 'you say' does the sound job.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook food slowly in a little liquid in a closed pot, a specific cooking method.

clue.text: Pub employee placing ban on nurse?

parts.note: to bar is to ban or prohibit
a tender is one who looks after or nurses someone

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pub worker is banning a nurse from the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placing ... on' sets the ban first, followed by the nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks behind a bar, so works for a pub.

clue.text: Mug with morning tea

parts.note: a mug is a fool or dupe, an ass
AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: A cup with a morning brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup to drink from but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea named after the Indian state where it grows.

clue.text: Frank beginning to snigger during ceremony? Not half

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of the word snigger

parts.note: during means in, as in the course of

indicators.note: Not half means the word ceremony loses half its letters, keeping only the front part

parts.note: the word ceremony in full, before it is cut down
half of the eight letters, the back four, are what go

explanation.surface: A man called Frank starts to snigger in the middle of a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective. 'beginning to' takes one letter, while 'Not half' keeps the first half, CERE, of CEREMONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank means speaking openly and honestly, which is what a sincere person does.

clue.text: Purpose of wrapping paper, provisionally

definitions.meaning: gift paper is there to wrap up a gift, so its purpose is to be used on a gift
for the time being, until something more permanent is settled

explanation.surface: Wrapping paper's purpose is stated, then a hedge that it is only temporary.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 'present' as a gift; the second takes it as the current moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means for now, temporarily, which is what provisionally means; read literally it names what gift wrap is meant for.

clue.text: Private meeting-places crammed together, for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all of the word is kept, here losing its final letter

parts.note: things packed tightly are dense

explanation.surface: Secret rendezvous spots are mostly packed tightly together.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a secluded room or lair where one retreats or meets privately, so the plural names such hideaways.

clue.text: American visiting Greek island given a light meal

indicators.note: visiting means one piece goes into another, as a visitor enters a place

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: An American tourist on a Greek island is served a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon snack of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a modest afternoon spread rather than a full meal, so it counts as a light meal.

clue.text: Girl ruined nice shirt

indicators.note: ruined suggests the letters of the two words are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A girl has spoiled a lovely shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Christine is a female given name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Some Neapolitans ignoring fellow from Rome?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people from Naples snub a man from Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Signor is the Italian title for a man, the equivalent of Mr, so an Italian fellow such as a Roman.

clue.text: One enigma, terribly fancy

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: terribly says the letters of the word enigma are badly arranged and must be sorted

explanation.surface: A single mystery, dreadfully elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy, in the sense of supposing or picturing something, is to imagine it.

clue.text: Smartly-dressed traveller wanting somewhere to sleep on way back

indicators.note: on way back means the combined letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: a rep, short for sales representative, is a commercial traveller
a pad is slang for a place to live and sleep

explanation.surface: A well-turned-out salesman needs a bed on his return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Dapper describes a man who is neat and trim in his clothes and appearance.

clue.text: Things grown for Mussolini

parts.note: pro means in favour of, or for
Il Duce, the leader, was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Crops grown on behalf of the Italian dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm produce is the crops and goods grown on the land.

clue.text: Reveller in vehicle crossing River Ouse

indicators.note: crossing means the vehicle spans the river, its letters going either side of the other pieces

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the Ouse is an English river, taken as written

explanation.surface: A partygoer is in a car driving over the River Ouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and another in East Anglia); 'crossing' has the vehicle straddle the river, which reads river first, then its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser drinks and makes merry noisily, which is what a reveller does.

clue.text: Scoundrel beheaded fish-eating creature

indicators.note: beheaded means the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a rotter is an old-fashioned word for a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain has been decapitated beside a fish-eating animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a river mammal that lives mainly on fish.

clue.text: City, unusually big, behold

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for unusually large sizes
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Look at this remarkably large city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Unsuccessful type protected by close relatives

indicators.note: protected by means the letters sit sheltered inside the words close relatives

explanation.surface: A failure is shielded by near family.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who habitually fails, an unsuccessful person.

clue.text: Health visitor is wrongly instructed, sir

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters are set out in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is told he has been given the wrong instructions by a medical visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link; the fodder is INSTRUCTED plus SIR. In Britain a district nurse visits patients at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A district nurse is a community nurse who makes home visits to patients, so a visitor concerned with health.

clue.text: Advice: where to put rubbish?

definitions.meaning: a useful hint or piece of guidance
a dump where refuse is taken

explanation.surface: Guidance on where to dispose of waste.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a tip is a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a piece of advice, and in British usage also a rubbish dump.

clue.text: Doctor accepting say extremely erudite qualification

indicators.note: accepting means the doctor takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, first and last, of the word erudite

explanation.surface: A doctor takes on, say, a very learned qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A university degree is an academic qualification awarded after a course of study.

clue.text: Attempt by US writer to produce verse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: An American author makes an effort at writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places the attempt beside the writer, which here means after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is writing in metrical lines, a synonym of poetry as a form.
